title: Exodus 13: By Strength of Hand the Lord Brought Us Out
body:
Read the chapter → [Exodus 13](/bible/exodus/13)

**[Exodus 13:1-2](/bible/exodus/13#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/exodus/13#v1)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/exodus/13#v2)</sup> Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Israel, both of man and of beast: it is mine.

- Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Israel, both of man and of beast: it is mine. The firstborn belong to the Most High.

**[Exodus 13:3-4](/bible/exodus/13#v3)**

> <sup>[3](/bible/exodus/13#v3)</sup> And Moses said unto the people, Remember this day, in which ye came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand the Lord brought you out from this place: there shall no leavened bread be eaten.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/exodus/13#v4)</sup> This day came ye out in the month Abib.

- Remember this day, in which ye came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand the Lord brought you out from this place, and no leavened bread is eaten.
- This day came ye out in the month Abib: the first month of the year, falling at the first new moon of the spring.

**[Exodus 13:5-10](/bible/exodus/13#v5)**

> <sup>[5](/bible/exodus/13#v5)</sup> And it shall be when the Lord shall bring thee into the land of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, which he sware unto thy fathers to give thee, a land flowing with milk and honey, that thou shalt keep this service in this month.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/exodus/13#v6)</sup> Seven days thou shalt eat unleavened bread, and in the seventh day shall be a feast to the Lord.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/exodus/13#v7)</sup> Unleavened bread shall be eaten seven days; and there shall no leavened bread be seen with thee, neither shall there be leaven seen with thee in all thy quarters.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/exodus/13#v8)</sup> And thou shalt shew thy son in that day, saying, This is done because of that which the Lord did unto me when I came forth out of Egypt.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/exodus/13#v9)</sup> And it shall be for a sign unto thee upon thine hand, and for a memorial between thine eyes, that the Lord’s law may be in thy mouth: for with a strong hand hath the Lord brought thee out of Egypt.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/exodus/13#v10)</sup> Thou shalt therefore keep this ordinance in his season from year to year.

- When the Lord brings Israel into the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, a land flowing with milk and honey, this service is kept in this month: seven days of unleavened bread, and in the seventh day a feast to the Lord, with no leaven seen in all thy quarters.
- Thou shalt shew thy son in that day, saying, This is done because of that which the Lord did unto me when I came forth out of Egypt. It is a sign upon thine hand and a memorial between thine eyes, that the Lord's law may be in thy mouth.
- Thou shalt therefore keep this ordinance in his season from year to year: the Passover is kept every year.

**[Exodus 13:11-13](/bible/exodus/13#v11)**

> <sup>[11](/bible/exodus/13#v11)</sup> And it shall be when the Lord shall bring thee into the land of the Canaanites, as he sware unto thee and to thy fathers, and shall give it thee,
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/exodus/13#v12)</sup> That thou shalt set apart unto the Lord all that openeth the matrix, and every firstling that cometh of a beast which thou hast; the males shall be the Lord’s.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/exodus/13#v13)</sup> And every firstling of an ass thou shalt redeem with a lamb; and if thou wilt not redeem it, then thou shalt break his neck: and all the firstborn of man among thy children shalt thou redeem.

- All that openeth the matrix is set apart unto the Lord; the matrix is the womb. Every firstling that cometh of a beast which thou hast, the males are the Lord's.
- Every firstling of an ass is redeemed with a lamb, and if not redeemed its neck is broken; and all the firstborn of man among thy children shalt thou redeem.

**[Exodus 13:14-16](/bible/exodus/13#v14)**

> <sup>[14](/bible/exodus/13#v14)</sup> And it shall be when thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, What is this? that thou shalt say unto him, By strength of hand the Lord brought us out from Egypt, from the house of bondage:
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/exodus/13#v15)</sup> And it came to pass, when Pharaoh would hardly let us go, that the Lord slew all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both the firstborn of man, and the firstborn of beast: therefore I sacrifice to the Lord all that openeth the matrix, being males; but all the firstborn of my children I redeem.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/exodus/13#v16)</sup> And it shall be for a token upon thine hand, and for frontlets between thine eyes: for by strength of hand the Lord brought us forth out of Egypt.

- When thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, What is this? thou shalt say, By strength of hand the Lord brought us out from Egypt, from the house of bondage: when Pharaoh would hardly let us go, the Lord slew all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, therefore the firstborn are sacrificed or redeemed.
- The children must be taught the righteousness of why the feast is kept. Ask the children of this land why they keep Christmas and they answer that Santa Claus is coming down the chimney; Israel's children are to be taught the works of the Most High instead.
- It is for a token upon thine hand and for frontlets between thine eyes, for by strength of hand the Lord brought us forth out of Egypt.

**[Exodus 13:17-18](/bible/exodus/13#v17)**

> <sup>[17](/bible/exodus/13#v17)</sup> And it came to pass, when Pharaoh had let the people go, that God led them not through the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for God said, Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt:
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/exodus/13#v18)</sup> But God led the people about, through the way of the wilderness of the Red sea: and the children of Israel went up harnessed out of the land of Egypt.

- When Pharaoh let the people go, God led them not through the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near, lest peradventure the people repent when they see war and return to Egypt. Israel would have been fearful at the sight of the Philistine army and turned back.
- The people felt a false security in Egypt: in the wilderness they murmured for the fish, the leeks, the onions, and the garlick of Egypt and loathed the light bread; and when the Assyrians came, Israel again ran down to Egypt for help. The same spirit holds the people in America today: a little job, government assistance, a car, food from the store, and they never want this kingdom to come down. But the Most High has something much greater in store: the world, the earth, and many mansions.
- So God led the people about, through the way of the wilderness of the Red Sea, and the children of Israel went up harnessed out of the land of Egypt.

  Precepts:
  - **[Numbers 11:5](/bible/numbers/11#v5)**
    > <sup>[5](/bible/numbers/11#v5)</sup> We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick:

    We remember the fish, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlick; the people longed for Egypt in the wilderness.
  - **[Numbers 21:5](/bible/numbers/21#v5)**
    > <sup>[5](/bible/numbers/21#v5)</sup> And the people spake against God, and against Moses, Wherefore have ye brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? for there is no bread, neither is there any water; and our soul loatheth this light bread.

    Our soul loatheth this light bread; the murmuring shows the false comfort Israel took in Egypt.
  - **[Isaiah 30:1-2](/bible/isaiah/30#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/isaiah/30#v1)</sup> Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord, that take counsel, but not of me; and that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin:
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/isaiah/30#v2)</sup> That walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt!

    Woe to the rebellious children that walk to go down into Egypt to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh; Israel kept running back to Egypt for safety.
  - **[John 14:2](/bible/john/14#v2)**
    > <sup>[2](/bible/john/14#v2)</sup> In my Father’s house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.

    In my Father's house are many mansions; the Most High has something far greater in store than the false security of this captivity.

**[Exodus 13:19](/bible/exodus/13#v19)**

> <sup>[19](/bible/exodus/13#v19)</sup> And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.

- Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for Joseph had straitly sworn the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.

**[Exodus 13:20-22](/bible/exodus/13#v20)**

> <sup>[20](/bible/exodus/13#v20)</sup> And they took their journey from Succoth, and encamped in Etham, in the edge of the wilderness.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/exodus/13#v21)</sup> And the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night:
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/exodus/13#v22)</sup> He took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, from before the people.

- They took their journey from Succoth and encamped in Etham, in the edge of the wilderness.
- The Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud to lead them the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, to go by day and night. He took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, from before the people.
